candidate.answerReason: The interval from boarding the morning bus to arriving home is 510 minutes. School occupies 450 minutes, leaving 60 minutes for both bus rides.

methods.label: Subtract school time from the whole interval
methods.explanation:
Start at \(7{:}30\) a.m., when Walter boards the first bus. From then until \(4{:}00\) p.m. is \(8\) hours \(30\) minutes, or
\[
8\cdot60+30=510\text{ minutes}.
\]
This interval consists of the two bus rides and his time at school.

His six classes take \(6\cdot50=300\) minutes, and the additional two hours take \(120\) minutes. Including lunch, his school time is
\[
300+30+120=450\text{ minutes}.
\]
Therefore, his total time on the bus is
\[
510-450=60\text{ minutes}.
\]
The answer is \(60\) minutes, choice B.
methods.levelReason: Only elapsed time, hour-to-minute conversion, and elementary arithmetic are needed.

candidate.annotationRationale: Elapsed time is the main target. The written method converts hours to minutes and treats bus time as the remaining part of a total interval. Its separate arithmetic steps do not require a general mixed-operation procedure or 24-hour notation.
